The dynamics between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy serve as the primary vehicle for exploring the novel's themes of social class and personal growth. Their initial mutual disdain highlights the rigid barriers of class and the prejudice that sustains them, while their gradual evolution toward respect and love demonstrates that these barriers can be overcome through self-reflection and the transformative power of genuine connection. This shift from misunderstanding to understanding underscores the theme that true social mobility and personal integrity require looking beyond superficial judgments.
